author: nsamaroo
text: Very nice! When scanning for trades, do you focus on a handful of pairs and look for a lot of different setups - or do you look through all pairs for a few setups when scanning? Hope that question makes sense to you. It does in my sleep deprived brain at the moment.

author: ShadowPit
text:
I am not too scientific about chart or trade selection as there are so many opportunities on every chart every day. When I first sit down I will click through around 20 pairs 1-by-1, pretty quickly, and eyeball the charts. Usually a chart will simply pop out to me before I get to the end of the 20 pairs and I'll drill deeper.

For example, in the chart above. It was a very common and obvious price setup which I am used to at a glance.: 1. There was a strong push down creating a pole. 2. In the middle of that sharp move down you can see the FL formed at the break of the low on the left. 3. You can observe clearly the price retracing and "engulfing" the FL to the left which forms the signal to go long at the decision point and/or QM level. 4. The only thing I had left to do was check that price was coming from a HTF demand and that was that. This is a very common setup that occurs within a few hours after high impact news events.

It ain't always that easy though, the majority of other trade setups I observe and take usually require far deeper investigation, they can often be more complex and not conforming to any specific price setup model like the one described above, they can also be time consuming to come to a decision on direction, and then require a lot of waiting for the right level, but this can all be managed with alerts, which I do use. But yeah, I hold no allegiance to any one pair or currency, but from my behaviour of scanning through 1-by-1 I usually end up trading the same pairs!

Unfortunately I don't really have any qualified advice for you. Given your fatigue, I might suggest you at least start small and note down 1-3 different setups you are comfortable with, like the one I have described above, and work on identifying those setups on 4 pairs only and pick those charts apart over the course of a week and reassess on the weekend whether you need more or not. It definitely helps to be well rested as well:)

Hello Whenever,

Blue box, a very rough idea of the key support/resistance on this timeframe. If I was to refine it further I would include the decision which engulfed the FL, which is where I have placed the 'ideal' stop in the chart below. But you get the rough idea right:)?

When you say lower line, did you mean why did I put the black horizontal line on top of the FL? I am not quite sure I follow your query, did I consider it for what?, if you don't mind can you be a bit more specific with your 3 thought bubbles regarding this? I haven't had my morning coffee yet I am sorry!

RE: stop placement - As I was late to the party for this trade, the stop placement was mainly to improve RR, I was even a bit generous on the spread with the logic that I used to place it. As price moves higher from HTF, I make the assumption new support will come into play where there was previous resistance. On an M1 chart, this obviously will result in a lower win rate over a larger sample size due to noisy nature of M1, but I am okay with that.
